question: Pandit Ravi Shankar popularised which instrument in particular all over the world?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sitar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Ravi Shankar **is renowned for popularizing the sitar, an Indian stringed instrument, globally. Shankar was a virtuoso of the sitar, an intricate instrument with a captivating resonance.
 
• Born on April 7, 1920, he commenced his performing career at the age of 14 as a dancer in his brother Uday's ensemble.
 
• Throughout the latter half of the 20th century, he ascended to become the foremost ambassador of North Indian classical music on the global stage.
 
• Shankar's artistic oeuvre encompasses a diverse range of endeavors, from composing pieces for orchestras to fusing clarinets with traditional Indian melodies, and even imparting sitar lessons to George Harrison, the guitarist of the Beatles.
 
• Additionally, he is the father of the acclaimed singer-songwriter Norah Jones.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The term **"sitar" **originates from the Persian word "sehtar," translating to "three-stringed." Believed to have evolved from long-necked lutes brought to India from Central Asia, the sitar reached its pinnacle during the 16th and 17th centuries before attaining its current form in the 18th century.
 
• **Tabla** comprises a pair of hand drums indigenous to the Indian subcontinent.
 
• **The veena** encompasses various chordophone instruments native to the Indian subcontinent.
 
• **Harmonium** resembles an organ and operates as a portable, hand-pumped reed organ, finding popularity across the Indian subcontinent.
